posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption:
We imagine advanced alien civilizations building gigantic spaceships, Dyson spheres and empires spanning entire galaxies. But what if true technological progress goes in exactly the opposite direction? Not outward into space, but deeper and deeper into the smallest layers of reality?

What is the Barrow Scale? How powerful could a civilization become by mastering DNA, and even fundamental particles, and could the universe already be filled with godlike civilizations hiding in plain sight? Watch
Let's visit some of the most dangerous neighbourhoods... in space!

Our curiosity to learn more about the stars is endless. Today, some scientists pursue their passion by building large telescopes that are able to capture the faintest glimmer of stars billions of light-years away. Some telescopes are even launched from Earth to get a clearer view outside the atmosphere. But what about the opportunity to see the stars with your own eyes, unfiltered? Astronauts, like the one that can be seen on the September page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, say nothing compa

Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

In the 17th century in Germany, one of Europe’s most terrifying witch hunts turned the town of Bamberg against itself. Tortures that occurred in the "Witch Factory" forced innocent people to name friends, neighbors and family members, creating a deadly chain reaction that eventually reached even the richest and most powerful, while those running the trials profited from the people they condemned.

competitors.bio: Discover the most incredible experiences from around the world 🌎✈️ Business: info@damiermedia.com

recentPosts.caption:
You don’t get many chances to have dinner inside a real airplane. ✈️⁠
⁠
The Airplane Restaurant in Colorado Springs turned a retired Boeing KC-97 tanker into a one-of-a-kind dining experience. ⁠
⁠
You can sit inside the aircraft, explore the space, and check out the aviation memorabilia throughout the restaurant while you eat.⁠
⁠
By: TheAirplaneRestaurant⁠

A tradition that has been keeping rice ready for the table for generations. 🌾✨⁠
An incredible glimpse of traditional rice cleaning, where grains are separated from husks and unwanted pieces using simple techniques passed down through generations.⁠
⁠
A beautiful piece of everyday culture you don’t get to see everywhere. 🌾⁠
Do you know where this traditional method is still used?⁠
🎥: @nisanighat

Even dogs ride scooters in Vietnam. 🐶⁠
⁠
From busy city streets to quiet neighborhoods, it’s common to spot dogs joining their owners for the ride.⁠
⁠
Some sit in front, some stand near their owners' legs, and others simply enjoy the view as they travel through the streets.⁠
⁠
By: @thomaster.p

A hidden side of Phuket that deserves to be discovered. 🌿✨⁠
@sunny_rung found this incredible spot where nature takes center stage, far from the usual beaches and busy city streets.⁠
⁠
Surrounded by lush greenery and paired with architecture that feels almost unreal, it’s the kind of place that makes you stop and take it all in. 🌴🏡⁠
🎥: @sunny_rung

Black sand beaches are some of the most unusual coastlines you’ll find around the world. 🖤🌊⁠
⁠
From volcanic shores in Hawaii and Japan to the dramatic coastline of New Zealand, these beaches get their dark color from volcanic rock and other natural materials.⁠
⁠
Save this list for the next time you’re looking for a beach that’s a little different.

A tiny Tokyo café with a 60-year story behind it. 🍮🇯🇵⁠
Hekkerun Coffee, a charming little shop run by 82-year-old Shizuo Mori, who has been making its famous homemade puddings for around six decades.⁠
⁠
Every morning starts at 4 AM to prepare the day’s puddings, and the demand says it all, visitors can wait hours in line, with the puddings sometimes selling out before closing time. 👀⁠
🎥: @mehtap.kurtel

Mashpi cloud forest in Ecuador. The Okavango Delta. Volcanoes National Park in Rwanda. Ngorongoro crater. Marrakesh. The Namib desert. The Great Barrier Reef. The Sacred Valley. Kyoto. Osa Peninsula. Baa Atoll.

Most people see a list like this and file it under someday, because a week at any of them runs into the thousands and the room is usually the biggest cost of the trip.

Unless you don’t pay for the room. Hotels have empty rooms every single night and they need content constantly, and a c

Pokémon fans, this one is for you. ⚡️⁠
⁠
PokéPark KANTO brings the world of Pokémon to life at Yomiuriland in Tokyo, with Pokémon Forest, Sedge Town, and plenty of familiar characters to spot along the way.⁠
⁠
Whether you grew up playing the games or just love Pokémon, this is a pretty fun place to see in Japan.⁠
⁠
By: @lyykevin

This tiny fish is a larval starry seabat. 🐟⁠
⁠
Photographed by @0311mg as it drifted in front of a diver’s mask, the fish is still in its early life stage. As it grows, it will transform into a bottom-dwelling seabat that uses its modified fins to move across the seafloor.

A hill near Porangahau in Hawke’s Bay, New Zealand, known also for its incredible Māori name,  and honestly, saying it might be half the experience. 😂⁠
The full name is Taumatawhakatangihangakoauauauotamateapokaiwhenuakitanatahu,  one of the longest place names in the world. ⁠
⁠
Think you can pronounce it?⁠
🎥: @yunru_

Spider lily season turns parts of Japan bright red every autumn. ⁠
⁠
Known as higanbana, or the “flower of the equinox,” these striking red flowers bloom around the autumn equinox, covering forests, fields, and riverbanks across the country.⁠
⁠
At Kinchakuda in Saitama, more than 5 million spider lilies bloom beneath the trees, creating one of Japan’s most spectacular autumn scenes.⁠
⁠
By: @travelwithaude

Okayyy, fried spider as a travel snack… anyone? 😂🕷️⁠
@spence.is.liquid gave us a taste of one of China’s more unusual street-food experiences, where fried spiders are served as a crunchy snack in some local markets.⁠
⁠
Would you actually try it? 👀

Presented by @Rolex. Welcome to Africa 🌍 Africa Earth’s Wild Home takes you deep into the heart of our wildest continent, bringing you closer to its animals, landscapes, and the people watching over it than ever before.

Through its partnership with the National Geographic Society and as part of its Perpetual Planet Initiative, #Rolex supports expeditions exploring and protecting remarkable places around the world, a selection of which are featured in Africa Earth’s Wild Home. #PerpetualPlanet

Describe Pompeii: Out of Time in 3 words? It's Now Streaming.

#PompeiiOutOfTime with @twhiddleston is now streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Experts define and treat ADHD as a single disorder, even though its symptoms can vary widely from one person to the next. Now, new brain imaging research suggests it may fall into three distinct "biotypes," offering a new explanation for why treatment can feel like trial and error.

Learn more about the three ADHD "biotypes" and what they could mean for the future at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Zephyr/Science Photo Library

A lion's mane jellyfish floats through the waters off York, Maine. The lion's mane is the largest species of jellyfish and can reach a diameter of 6.6 feet (2 meters) with tentacles that can exceed 49 feet (15 meters). 🪼

Photograph by @brianskerry.

Photo by @anton.linstrom | Turgen Jailoo, nestled in the Tian Shan ranges of Kyrgyzstan, is a remote alpine valley where emerald meadows meet snowcapped mountains. During my journey across Kyrgyzstan, I camped here among wild horses and winding rivers, capturing the untouched beauty of this highland landscape.

This photo was featured in our @natgeoyourshot #NatGeoYourShotBOTW2026 challenge.

POV: You're witnessing one of North America's largest marine migrations from within. Each year, striped mullet stream through Florida’s waters to reach their spawning grounds in schools so vast that they can darken the shallow waters. Filmed by photographer and National Geographic Explorer @macstonephoto, these runs have become even more spectacular over the years, in part thanks to conservation efforts that have benefited other species too. 

Find out more about this incredible marine migration

“Frozen shoulder” is a real condition causing stiffness and difficulty in raising the arm. It mostly affects women, striking peri- or post-menopausal women more commonly than anyone else. The painful affliction can last for years—but has long been ignored by medical researchers who doubted its existence. New treatments may finally promise a cure.

Learn more about frozen shoulder and how it might finally be addressed at the link in bio.

Photograph by K H Fung, Science Photo Library

Some snowy mountain tops to bring some beauty to your day. 🗻

Photograph by @renan_ozturk

While searching for anteaters at night, Nat Geo Explorer @fernando.faciole spotted the glowing eyes of caimans, reptiles in the alligator family that are commonly found in the Brazilian Pantanal.

Learn more about what it took to capture his story on the elusive giant anteaters of Brazil at the link in bio.

With decades of experience behind them, older female orcas are often the pod's most valuable leaders. Even once they've reached menopause, they play a crucial part in helping their family survive. 

#NatGeoQueens is streaming on @DisneyPlus and @hulu.

Meet Agbaibor, a critically endangered African forest elephant. At around eight months old, he was found wandering alone near Nigeria's Okomu National Park, a highly unusual sight since elephant calves typically stay with their mothers until they're weaned at around two to three years old. It's unclear how he became separated from his family, but after being transported to a nearby ranger outpost, he became the first case of elephant rescue in the country.

Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD), a form of PMS that can trigger severe depression, intense anxiety, and other debilitating physical and psychological symptoms, affects around 3 to 8 percent of women of reproductive age. For decades, experts thought it was caused by hormonal imbalances, but a new body of research tells a more nuanced story—reshaping not just our understanding of the condition but how it can be treated.

The critically endangered Tenkile is found only in Papua New Guinea's Torricelli Mountains, where local communities have played a vital role in protecting this remarkable tree kangaroo. Seeing one caught on camera in the wild is a hopeful sign for its future!
